dataset_family: I-CONECT (Internet-Based Conversational Engagement Clinical Trial, NCT02871921; Portland OR / Detroit MI); four themes with 29-36 participants each
method_family: Multimodal embedding-level fusion: wav2vec speech + BERT transcript + Video Swin facial video, three pairs of parallel co-attention blocks in a cross-transformer, MLP classifier; 10-fold CV repeated 5 times
what_it_shows: The data are interviewer-led semi-structured webcam video chats from the I-CONECT trial: facial video, participant audio and ASR transcripts. With all three modalities fused, 10-fold CV repeated 5 times gives per-theme accuracy of 84.2-89.3% and AUC of 82.7-85.3%, in 29-36 participants per theme. Vision alone gives 67.9-71.2% accuracy (AUC 60.3-64.1), and speech alone is at chance (AUC 48.8-55.7). There is no external validation and no head-to-head against a specialist instrument.
why: Poor, Dodge and Mahoor 2024, Computers in Biology and Medicine 182:109199. The PDF title and authors match the block content (multimodal cross-transformer on I-CONECT speech/language/vision, average AUC 85.3%), and the DOI matches the map. The block has no Title/Authors fields. Read in full; the reference list is omitted from the extract. TABLE A1: PARTLY. It shows consumer-grade capture ('the Internet and a user-friendly device/webcam', p.5) and high standalone accuracy, with 89.3% best theme and 84-89% across all four (Table 2, p.8). It is NOT self-administered: 'semi-structured conversations with interviewers' (p.5). NARROWED WORDING: YES on content. Low-cost behavioural data from home video-chat interviews in the US trial cohort gives a best-case standalone accuracy of 89.3%, with the other themes at 84.2-87.3%, in small internally cross-validated samples, with no external validation and no specialist comparator. This is the kind of evidence the narrowed wording describes. It would be a THIRD analysis of the same cohort, and its in-band result needs audio and transcripts as well as facial video (vision-only 67.9-71.2%). INDEPENDENCE: it adds NO dataset family. It is the same I-CONECT cohort as supporters P-76 and P-77 and candidate P-6. It shares authors Hiroko H. Dodge and Mohammad H. Mahoor with P-76 (Sun, Dodge, Mahoor), P-77 (Alsuhaibani, Dodge, Mahoor) and P-6. It reuses P-76's first author's frame-extraction pipeline ('a sequence-based approach proposed by Sun et al.', p.5; 'We would like to thank Mr. Jian Sun for the video frames extraction', p.10). Under Appendix H.1 it could replace P-76 or P-77 as the I-CONECT representative, but it cannot raise the count. The review's I-CONECT family stays one dataset. CAUTIONS: accuracy exceeds AUC in three of four themes, and the standard deviations across five repeated 10-fold runs are very small (AUC +/-0.5-0.8 points) for 29-36 subjects. No separate validation set is described ('trained using 10-fold cross-validation on every theme and tested on the respective test set'). REGISTRY DEFECT: Sample_N_Approx 155 is the number of trial participants who started the intervention or control arms. The analysed samples are 29-36 per theme (Table 1, p.7), and the control arm was not used.

quotes.quote: The participants in the experimental group engaged in semi-structured conversations with interviewers prompted by daily themes and associated pictures 4 times per week for 6 months and twice per week for an additional 6 months. Each session consists of 30 min of conversations using the Internet and a user-friendly device/webcam.
